The following enhancements were made to the Incidents page:

blocks.item: In the incidents table, the following columns are added:
Triggered Dictionary Matches: The aggregate match count for all triggered DLP dictionaries for the incident.
Total Dictionary Matches: The aggregate match count for all triggered and non-triggered dictionary matches for the incident.

In the Filters window, the following filters are added:
To use these filters, select to include or exclude a range of matches by selecting an operator (>, ≥, <, ≤, or =) and the number of matches (e.g., > 20, ≥ 20, < 100, ≤ 100, or = 25)).

blocks.text: To learn more, see Managing Incidents and Using Incident Filters in Workflow Automation.

On the Notification Template page, you can create custom email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams notification templates that your organization can use. When creating these different types of templates, you can use the merge tags that Workflow Automation provides to include incident attribute values in the notifications. The same merge tags are available for all formats of notification templates. The following image shows the new merge tag when configuring a Slack template.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Notification Templates, Adding Email Notification Templates, Adding Slack Notification Templates, and Adding Microsoft Teams Notification Templates.
On the Incidents page, two new actions are added to the Actions drop-down menu, and you can perform these actions against multiple incidents. These actions are:

blocks.item: Delete: You can use this action to delete incidents in any status.
Email Release Quarantine: You can use this action to release quarantined emails to their recipients for incidents of Source DLP type Email.

blocks.heading: Modifications to the Incident Details Drawer

blocks.text: On the Incident Details drawer, the content is modified on the Overview tab and the Violation Details tab. The following modifications were made:

blocks.item: The Overview section title is removed. The overview information still appears at the top of the tab without a section title.

The Current State Details section is removed. The fields that were in that section (Status and User) are now in the overview information at the top of the tab. The Status field is the first field that appears in the overview information before the Incident ID field, and the User field appears after the Priority field.
The Violation Details section title is removed.
Some of the fields in the overview information on the Overview tab are also displayed at the top of this tab. This partial overview information appears at the top of the tab without a section title.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details.

blocks.heading: Support for Shared Credentials with Internet & SaaS When Configuring Azure DLP Application Integrations Using Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding

blocks.text: You can configure an Azure DLP application integration using cloud-to-cloud incident forwarding to use shared credentials between Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Workflow Automation (i.e., Azure certificate-based authentication). If you choose to use shared credentials between Internet & SaaS and Workflow Automation, you must onboard an Azure application tenant in Internet & SaaS using a private key, and the tenant must be onboarded for Workflow Automation. After you onboard the Azure application tenant, the system automatically adds a new Azure DLP application integration in Disabled state for you in Workflow Automation. To use this integration in Workflow Automation, you must enable it on the edit Zscaler DLP Azure Integration page in Workflow Automation.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Azure DLP Application Integration Using Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding and Configuring DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding for Microsoft Azure.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to Privacy Settings for DLP Application Integrations

blocks.text: On the add Zscaler DLP Integration page, the add Zscaler DLP Azure Integration page, and the add Zscaler DLP GCP Integration page, three additional privacy settings are added. These privacy settings are:

blocks.item: Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - Admin: Select this privacy setting if you do not want the admins to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident on the Violation Details tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can view these sections of the policy details for the incident. This privacy setting is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - Admin privacy setting.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - End User: Select this privacy setting if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view these sections of the policy details for the incident. This privacy setting is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - End User privacy setting.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - Manager/Approver: Select this privacy if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view these sections of the policy details for the incident. This privacy setting is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - Manager/Approver privacy setting.

blocks.heading: Enhancements to the Incident Details Drawer

blocks.text: The following enhancements were made to the Incident Details drawer:

blocks.item: At the top of the drawer, you can use the Next Incident and Previous Incidents icons to navigate through the list of incidents that are displayed on the Incidents page.

You can change the default tab that appears when the Incident Details drawer opens by clicking the star icon next to one of the tab headings in the Incident Details drawer. The Overview tab initially appears, by default. A blue star indicates the default tab. This tab setting is stored in your browser's local storage so that your change is preserved for the next time you log on. If you clear your cache or use a different browser, this setting is lost.
After you close the Incident Details drawer, the system automatically refreshes the Incidents page.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details.

blocks.heading: Enhancements to the Incident Details Drawer for Incidents of Source DLP Type Email

blocks.text: The following enhancements were made to the Incident Details drawer:

blocks.item: On the Violation Details tab, in the Policy section, the dictionaries and engines are displayed that triggered the incident because of the content of the email subject line, the email body, or the email attachments associated with the incident. The Policy section is redesigned to contain an Email Subject tab, an Email Body tab, and an Email Attachments tab. In the Email Attachments tab, a subtab appears for each attachment that caused a violation.

On the Violation Content tab, the View Trigger Data section is enhanced to display the trigger data for the different types of violations triggered by the different DLP dictionaries associated with an incident. This section is also redesigned to contain an Email Subject tab, an Email Body tab, and an Email Attachments tab. In the Email Attachments tab, a subtab appears for each attachment that caused a violation. In this section, you can view the dictionaries and the exact data that violated the DLP policies.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details.

On the Notification Template page, you can create custom email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams notification templates that your organization can use. When creating these different types of templates, you can use the merge tags that Workflow Automation provides to include incident attribute values in the notifications. The following additional merge tags are added:

blocks.item: A combination of file name and file size.

blocks.text: The same merge tags are available for all formats of notification templates. The following images show the new merge tags when configuring a Slack template.

In this section, you can view the dictionaries and the exact data that violated the DLP policies.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details.

blocks.item: This endpoint provides the quarantine email release status for the recipients. Statuses are quarantined, failed, in progress, and success.

On the custom workflow builder page, a new Configure Notify Node window is added. This window is conversation based and assists you with configuring a Notify node for a user notification or an escalation notification in a custom workflow. After you click the Notify tile and drag and drop it to the custom workflow design area, this window appears.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Workflows.

blocks.heading: Time Zone Selection for Time-Related Merge Tags on Notifications

blocks.text: You can select the time zone in which the time-related merge tags appear on a user or escalation notification that are created manually or through a workflow. There are several ways to select the time zone. You can select the time zone:

blocks.item: On the Incident Details page, when you perform the Notify User or Escalate action for an incident.
On the custom workflow builder page, when you configure a workflow with a notify tile for a user or escalation notification.
On the Notification Template page, when you configure an email, Slack, or Microsoft Teams notification template.
On the Add or Edit Admin Assignment window, when you add or edit an admin assignment.

blocks.text: If you do not select the time zone using any of these pages or windows, then the system uses the UTC+00:00 time zone, by default.
To learn more, see Viewing and Managing Incident Details, Managing Workflows, Managing Notification Templates, and Managing Admin Assignments.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to the Export Incidents Feature

blocks.text: On the Incidents page, you can export the incidents that are displayed on the page to a CSV file. For incidents that have duplicate incidents, the CSV file lists the main incident ID along with each of the duplicate incident IDs in the Transaction ID field. The incident IDs are separated by a comma.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Incidents.

blocks.heading: Modification to the Duplicate Incident Logic

blocks.text: The duplicate incident logic is modified to not require the MD5 hash value for incidents resulting from rules without content inspection (i.e., the Engines attribute value is External DLP).
To learn more, see Understanding Duplicate Incidents in Workflow Automation.

blocks.heading: Workflow Automation Integration with SaaS Security Posture Management

blocks.text: Workflow Automation supports integration with SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM). This integration enables you to configure workflows that automatically trigger tickets for SSPM controls and findings through a SaaS application ticketing system (i.e., ServiceNow). In SSPM, the workflows that you configure in Workflow Automation are manually triggered when an admin clicks the Add Ticket icon next to a control or finding that is captured in SSPM.

As a result of the integration, the manual ticket-creation process for SSPM controls and findings is simplified. Reducing the ticket creation time results in faster remediation and clear ownership of SSPM controls and findings.
This feature is in limited availability. To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see:

blocks.item: Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Workflow Automation for SSPM Controls and Findings
Accessing and Navigating the Workflow Automation Admin Portal for SSPM Controls and Findings

blocks.text: On the Incident Details page opened in a new tab from the Incidents page, you can perform actions on the incident on this page, and you can click the Refresh button at the top of the page to display the latest information for the incident.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to the Quarantined Email Release Feature

blocks.text: On the Incident Details page, for an email incident with a quarantined status, after you release the quarantined email to one or more of its recipients, the Quarantined Email Status field appears in the Overview section on this page. When you click the View Status link in this field, the Quarantined Email Status page appears. On this page, you can view the status of the quarantine release for each of the recipients.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details.

blocks.heading: Update to Supported Number of Predicates for Statements for Incident Group and Workflow Mappings

blocks.text: On the Incident Group Mapping page and the Workflow Mappings page, you configure the mappings for incident groups or workflows, respectively, by adding statements (i.e., rules). Each statement contains one or more predicates. You can add up to 100 predicates for a statement.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Incident Group Mappings and Managing Workflow Mappings.

blocks.text: On the Incidents page and the Incident Analytics dashboard, a Response Available widget is added. This widget displays the number of incidents where a user has provided a response from a user notification, or where a manager or approver has provided a response from an escalation notification (i.e., incidents with the status Received Justification Response).

blocks.heading: Enhancement to the Incident Details Page

blocks.text: On the Incidents Details page, you can manually create a policy exception for an incident by selecting the Create Policy Exception action. When creating the policy exception, you enter the duration for the policy exception using days, hours, and minutes. Previously, the duration could only be entered in minutes.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details.

blocks.heading: Enhancements to the Incident Summary Page

blocks.text: A couple of enhancements were made to the Incident Summary page. These enhancements are:

blocks.item: The Incident Summary page is now a stand-alone page. Previously, it was accessed from the Incidents page.

On the Incident Summary page, when you click a link that appears in the Incident Summary table, a new tab opens, displaying the Selected Criteria page. This page displays the criteria associated with the link in the Selected Criteria section of the page, and lists the actual incidents with the relevant filters applied for that combination of criteria. Each link you click in the Incident Summary table opens a new tab, and the tab stays open until you close it.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see Managing Incident Summaries.

The merge tags that are available when configuring a notification template depend upon the type of notification template you are configuring. Different sets of merge tags are available for a user or escalation notification template versus an end user or admin digest notification template. The following images are examples of the merge tags for the different types of notification templates.

blocks.text: If you have existing notification templates that are configured with the merge tags that are no longer available for that particular notification type, an error message is shown when you attempt to edit those templates.

In Workflow Automation, there are a few pages (e.g., the Approvers page, Integration Users page, Incident Details page, and custom workflows page) that require you to enter an email address, and you must enter email addresses when importing user attributes using a CSV file on the Import CSV page. In addition, email addresses are displayed on a few of the pages (e.g., Incidents page, Incident Summary page, and Incident Details page) in Workflow Automation. Email addresses are enhanced throughout to support apostrophes (e.g., john.o’mailley@companyabc.com and k’lynn.brown@companyabc.com) and hyphenated characters (e.g., susan.smith-jones@companyabc.com and mary-lou.johnson@companyabc.com).
The following image shows examples of email addresses with apostrophes and hyphenated characters on the Approvers page.
See image.

On the Incidents page, Incident Summary page, and the Incident Analytics dashboard, you can filter the incidents that appear by selecting the time range. The custom date range option is enhanced to enable you to specify the time (i.e. hour, minute, and second) for the start date and the end date.

Component: The specific subresource within a SaaS tenant where the incident violation occurred.
Content Location: The category of the collaboration channel for the event.
Workspace: The name or identifier of the collaboration workspace.
Domains: The list of domains associated with the incident transaction context.
In addition, when you export incidents, these new columns appear in the incident export file, and in the Filters window, these attributes are added as filter options.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to the Incidents Page and Incident Details Page

blocks.text: On the Incidents page and the Incident Details page, a Refresh button is added to the top of the page. When you click this button, the system reloads the page and displays the latest information.
See image.

The following are enhancements to the Data Protection features in Workflow Automation:

On the Incident Summary page, you can view aggregate incident counts for a specified date range by using various selectable attributes and filters. Workflow Automation provides several attributes that you can use to summarize the number of the incidents that have occurred in your organization.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Incident Summaries.

Workflow Automation creates an audit log when you click the Generate Presigned Link for an incident in the Violation Content section on the Incident Details page. You can view this audit log on the Audit Logs page.
See image.

Workflow Automation enables you to create a policy exception for an Inline Source DLP type incident for a specified period of time. You can create a policy exception for an incident using one of the following methods:

blocks.item: On the Incident Details page, you can select the Create Policy Exception action from the Actions drop-down menu and specify the period of time for the policy exception.

On the custom workflow builder page, you can configure a custom workflow so that a policy exception can be applied to an incident through an escalation notification or user notification. A Policy Exception tile is added to the custom workflow builder.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing & Managing Incident Details and Managing Workflows.

Workflow Automation can send notification reminders to end users, managers, and approvers who have previously received user or escalation notifications for incidents but have not yet responded to those notifications. On the Account Settings page, you can configure who is to receive these reminders and the frequency at which they are sent.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Account Settings and Understanding Notification Reminders.

blocks.heading: Support for Releasing Quarantined Emails for Email Incidents

blocks.text: Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) incidents that Microsoft has quarantined are displayed in Workflow Automation. In Workflow Automation, you can release the email to one or more of its recipients using one of the following methods:

blocks.item: On the Incident Details page, an admin can select the Release Email Quarantine action from the Actions drop-down menu and select the recipients to release the email to.

When a user responds to an end user notification or an escalation notification that is associated with a quarantined email incident, the notifications are enhanced to include a new Release Email to Recipients section that includes release quarantine options.

blocks.text: To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.
